issues.description: sign_message silently maps unknown SigningMode values to CHIP_0002 while verify_signature raises
issues.detail: The two halves of the new chia/wallet/util/signing.py disagree on unknown-mode handling: sign_message falls through to CHIP_0002 UTF-8 in its else branch, verify_signature raises ValueError. Pick one policy and apply it symmetrically; silent fallthrough hides caller bugs in a freshly extracted library.

issues.description: SigningMode-to-bytes encoding table is duplicated between sign_message and verify_signature
issues.detail: Both functions re-implement the same four-branch mode-to-message-bytes mapping with subtly different groupings and defaults. Extract a single pure helper (e.g. _encode_message(mode, message)) so divergence is impossible and the CHIP-0002 comment lives in one place.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum exists as both a VerifySignature property and a free function with different inputs
issues.detail: VerifySignature.signing_mode_enum parses a string; the new module-level signing_mode_enum(request) derives a mode from (is_hex, safe_mode) booleans. Same name, different semantics, inconsistent placement across sibling request types. Rename one (e.g. derive_signing_mode_from_flags) or unify the shape across all request dataclasses.

issues.description: signing util imports VerifySignatureResponse from wallet_request_types, inverting layering
issues.detail: A utility module should not depend on RPC wire types. Either move VerifySignatureResponse down into the util, or have verify_signature return a plain (bool, str|None) and let the RPC layer wrap it. As written, every consumer of the util drags in RPC request-types.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring is a stale stub referencing a nonexistent :param request:
issues.detail: The function now takes explicit keyword args (signing_mode, public_key, message, signature, address) but the docstring still says ':param request:' from its prior life as an RPC handler. Either describe the actual parameters and error contract or delete the stub; a wrong docstring is worse than none.

issues.description: New tests verify the signer in isolation and never assert the RPC response's isValid flag
issues.detail: test_sign_message_by_nft_id calls AugSchemeMPL.verify directly across four near-identical branches instead of round-tripping through the new verify_signature() and parametrizing over (is_hex, safe_mode, encoder). test_sign_message_by_address discards verify_signature's return, so a False isValid would pass silently. Add the round-trip assertion and table-drive the cases.

synthesis.summary: The extract-to-library is the right shape and the new tests for sign_message_by_id close a real coverage gap. But the new chia/wallet/util/signing.py ships avoidable rough edges: sign_message and verify_signature disagree on unknown-mode handling (silent fallthrough vs ValueError), the SigningMode-to-bytes table is duplicated across both functions, and signing_mode_enum exists as both a VerifySignature property and a free function with different semantics. A layering inversion has the util importing VerifySignatureResponse from the RPC request-types module. The verify_signature docstring is a stale request-object stub, and tests verify the signer directly rather than round-tripping through the new util. NEEDS-WORK before landing on the symmetry and layering; the rest are cleanups worth doing while the file is open.
